name: dd
summary: Copy and convert raw data streams.
description: Copies data using configurable block sizes and conversions; use carefully because it writes raw devices without confirmation.

options.description: Read from FILE instead of standard input.
Read and write BYTES at a time.

examples.title: Create a raw image copy
examples.output:
16+0 records in
16+0 records out
67108864 bytes copied
examples.explanation: Copies an image using a larger block size and progress reporting.

examples.title: Write a fixed-size zero file
examples.command: dd if=/dev/zero of=blank.bin bs=1M count=4 status=none
examples.explanation: Creates a four-megabyte file of zero bytes.

examples.title: Inspect a boot signature
examples.command: dd if=disk.img bs=512 count=1 status=none | hexdump -C | head -n 1
examples.explanation: Reads only the first sector for inspection.

warnings: dd writes raw bytes with no prompt and no undo; pointing of= at the wrong target (for example a disk device) overwrites the data that is there.
